concept.name: Read-only trading agent
concept.definition: A trading agent whose tool permissions are restricted to data retrieval and computation — market data, knowledge bases, analytics — with no capability to submit, modify, or cancel orders. It operationalizes the least-privilege principle: the system's action space is limited to the minimum necessary for its function, so even malfunction or prompt injection cannot move money.
concept.intuition: An analyst with a terminal and no trading button: it can look everything up and tell you what it thinks, but it physically cannot place a trade.
concept.mechanics: The agent's declared tool set contains only query/compute functions; the broker or exchange connection either has no API credentials for order entry or routes through an account with trading disabled. Because enforcement is in credentials and infrastructure rather than instructions, no prompt — user or injected — can escalate its privileges.
concept.failure_modes: The safety property fails if the 'read-only' boundary is implemented in the prompt or application layer rather than in credentials, or if read access itself leaks sensitive data (positions, strategies) to injected instructions. Read-only agents can still cause harm through wrong analysis that a human acts on.
concept.misconceptions: Read-only does not mean harmless — outputs still influence decisions, and data access still needs scoping. It also is not a compromise on usefulness for many roles: research, review, and coaching agents need no order capability at all.
concept.example: A knowledge agent answers 'walk me through the margin math on this spread' using market-data and library lookups; its API token has trading disabled at the broker, so no prompt it receives can result in an order.

citations.source: OWASP, 'LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection' (OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications)
citations.section: Prevention and Mitigation Strategies, item 4 (privilege control and least-privilege access)
